newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 16.

text.p: CSX Corp agreed to buy Conrail Inc for cash and stock together worth $8.1 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
- Berkshire Hathaway agreed to buy Flightsafety International for $1.5 billion.
- Archer Daniels Midland Co has become an ally of U.S. prosecutors in their anitrust investigation into price fixing among it and its competitors.
- European Union will support Eastman Kodak Co's trade complaint against Japan and Fuji Photo Film Co in joining the United States in its case before the World Trade Organization.
- U.S. federal appeals court in Kansas City, Mo, temporarily halted important parts of the Federal Communications Commission's order setting rules to foment competition in local telephone markets.
- Chase Manhattan Corp, Citibank and NationsBank Corp enjoyed strong quarterly results compared to the same period last year.
- General Motors Corp nearly doubled its quarterly earnings from the previous year.
- Coca-Cola Co's quarterly profit rose 21 percent on one-time gains, while PepsiCo Inc had a 77-percent net income drop.
- Chrysler Corp plans to increase its capacity by 14 percent by 1999 as part of a five-year plan.
- Caterpillar Inc saw quarterly profits climb 46 percent on strong U.S. sales.
- Sun Microsystems Inc saw its quarterly profit surge 46 percent on strong demand for its computers.
- Amgen Inc reported a 23-percent rise in quarterly profit amid news of poor test results of a new drug.
- Brokerage houses Merrill Lynch, PaineWebber and Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette had better than expected quarterly results.
- The firm that the Federal Bureau of Investigation created for its sting operation against alleged stock manipulators appears to be Thorton Capital.
- The Dow Jones industrial average fell 5.22 points to close at 6,004.78 a day after it closed above the 6,000 mark.
- Some people on Wall Street expect David Johnson, head of Campbell Soup Co, to tell the company's annual meeting next month whether he will stay on after his contract expires in July.
China, Japan, Germany and Saudi Arabia are buying up U.S. government bonds following the Federal Reserve's decision not to raise interest rates.
